This column is to remind you of one such story, a story that began in 1982 in Arunachal Pradesh, a state about which we know precious little, barring the fact that it borders China. items.title: Tryst with the Constitution: Parliament must debate
items.summary: In his final address to the Constituent Assembly, Dr BR Ambedkar famously remarked that the success of a Constitution depends, in large measure, on the people who are called upon to work it. If they happen to be a ‘good lot’, even a bad Constitution may turn out to be good. The functioning of the Constituent Assembly, the intellectual rigour of its deliberations and, more importantly, the attitude of its members proved that they were indeed such ‘good people’. 77 years later, as we celebrate Constitution Day, we must revisit the spirit of deliberation that characterised the making of our Constitution. Deliberation, dissent, consensus A remarkable feature of the Indian Constitution is the extent to which it was discussed and debated before it took its final shape. Prior to the appointment of the Drafting Committee, the Assembly constituted numerous committees to examine specific aspects of the Constitution and make recommendations. These recommendations, as approved by the Assembly, formed the basis of the initial draft prepared by Sir BN Rau, which was subsequently scrutinised and revised by the Drafting Committee led by Dr Ambedkar. items.summary: A Delhi court on Monday acquitted Harish M Bhatia, former CEO of My FM, the radio arm of the Dainik Bhaskar Group, of the charges of outraging and insulting the modesty of a woman. Judicial Magistrate First Class Shivangi Vyas of Saket courts held that the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubt. The Court reiterated that a conviction in a sexual offence can be based solely n a complainant's testimony only if the same is of sterling quality. "The conviction in a sexual offence case can be based solely on the testimony of prosecutrix provided her testimony is of sterling quality that is wholly reliable, consistent and inspires confidence," it said. Where the case rests primarily on that testimony, the Court must scrutinize it with greater care to ensure that it is free from material contradictions, improvements, omissions or inherent improbabilities, the judge added. Since the same was not satisfied in the present case, Bhatia was acquitted of all charges.
